question: is the published expression-to-growth law testable with LOCAL data? It needs promoter strength PAIRED WITH growth rate on the same rows.
method: READ-ONLY header scan. Fetched nothing. A file qualifies only if its header carries BOTH an expression-like and a growth-like token -- the PAIRING is the requirement, not the presence of either axis somewhere in the repo. Tokens are matched against header fields SPLIT on non-alphanumerics, not by substring.
defect_found_and_fixed_during_this_step: The first version SUBSTRING-matched and returned pairing-found on three files. All three were FALSE POSITIVES whose only growth hit was 'rate' inside num_integ-RATE-d_barcodes; none carries a growth or fitness axis at all -- they are RNA counts, DNA counts and barcode tallies. The verdict INVERTED on the fix. Same defect class this repo has recorded before, where a word-boundary assumption failed on a real column name. Caught by inspecting the three candidates instead of accepting the verdict, which the probe's own honest-limits had flagged as the non-conservative direction.
detail: 2 reachable root(s), 46 tabular files examined, and NONE carries an expression-like column alongside a growth-like column on the same rows. The law relates the two, so expression-only substrates (GSE108535) and growth-only substrates (FBA/Keio) each fail it separately.
why_a_vacuous_pass_is_impossible: An empty inventory yields substrate-blocked, never a clean pass; and if NO root were readable the verdict is indeterminate rather than blocked, because unreadable roots cannot support a claim about what exists.
honest_limits: HEADER scan only. A dataset pairing the two axes across two files joined by a key would NOT be detected, and neither would one whose columns are named unconventionally.
Per-root scan bounded to the first 400 tabular files; the per-root count is reported so truncation is visible.

Token matching is lexical. 'rate' is deliberately in the growth list and will also match unrelated rate columns, which biases this probe toward FINDING a pairing -- so a substrate-blocked verdict is the conservative direction.
The one source that could have said whether such a paired dataset exists in the literature (the eLife random-promoter paper) was UNREACHABLE from this host.
